Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had a big white hat and white shoes. She was so happy.

One day she went for a walk in the park and something strange happened. In the lake she saw a monster! It was a big white monster with lots of eyes and teeth.

The little girl was so scared and she wanted to run away, but then she decided to be brave. She stomped her feet and clapped her hands. The monster got scared and it ran away!

The little girl was so happy. She clapped her hands and said, "Yay!" She was so brave.

The End.

Once there was a little girl who was curious. Whenever she saw something new, she wanted to try it. One day, she found a furry thing on the floor. She thought it was very interesting. She picked it up and said to herself, â€œWhat is this?â€

Just then, her mom came up to her. She saw the small, furry object and said, â€œThatâ€™s a match.â€ The little girl looked confused. â€œWhat does it do?â€ she asked.

â€œWell, itâ€™s used to make a fire in a sinkâ€, her mom replied. The little girl thought for a moment before she said, â€œOh. Like when we cook food?â€

Her mom smiled. â€œYes, exactly.â€ She took the match from the little one and lit it with her thumb. â€œSee, now it will help us cook.â€ 

The little girl liked playing with the furry match. She watched as her mom used it to light the fire in the sink. She clapped happily, excited to learn something new.

Once upon a time there was an ancient spot in the forest. A little girl named Molly took a trip to the spot to see what it was like. As she looked around, she saw that it was very old and seemed to be magical.

"What is this place?" said Molly to a nearby bird.

The bird chirped and then said, "This is an ancient spot. It has been here for many, many years."

Molly was interested in the spot so she decided to stand right in the center of it. Suddenly, she felt a tingle pass through her body.

"What was that?" said Molly, feeling a bit scared.

The bird said, "That was the magic of this spot. It will give you strength."

Molly was surprised, but also excited. She thanked the bird and then stood in the spot for a few moments more, feeling the strength it gave her. Then she waved goodbye and left the ancient spot.

Mary and her brother Sam love to play together. One day they decided to clap their hands and see who could clap the loudest. Sam clapped extra loudly, and Mary clapped extra fast. 

Mama heard the noise and came in to see what was going on. She saw Mary and Sam clapping, and she smiled.

Mama said, "You two were being very naughty, but because you were having fun I will give you each a cookie!"

With that, Mary and Sam stopped clapping and each one grabbed a cookie. They were both very happy. 

Mama said that from now on, they had to be good whenever they clapped because it was too loud. Mary and Sam agreed, giggling and eating their cookies. 

The two had so much fun together, and Mama was happy to see them happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Pam. She was very shy and never liked to be around a lot of people.

So each day, Pam would take a walk in a special place, a field near her home. Every day when she walked in this field, she'd take a sack with her.

One day, as Pam was walking in the field, she heard something strange. It was like a horn calling out - faint noises coming from a far distance. After a while, Pam recognised the sound; it was her pet donkey, Jack.

Pam was very excited - she had been looking for Jack since the morning! She quickened her pace and soon she could see him, running and jumping in the meadow. She ran towards him and hugged him.

"You're finally here!" Pam said, relieved and happy. "Where have you been? You fit quite well in this field!"

Jack smiled and looked content. Pam was sure that from now on, this would be his favorite spot in the world!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sandy who was always looking for adventure. One day, Sandy decided to go explore a quiet valley nearby. She walked and walked until she reached the valley. When she got there, Sandy was in for a big surprise. 

In the middle of the valley was a big tree with a strange box beneath it! Sandy was very curious and opened it - she found a big pile of sweets inside! Her eyes were wide with joy. 

Suddenly, another little girl appeared on the other side of the valley. She saw the box and ran towards it too. Sandy and the other girl started to fight for the candy. Sandy wasn't sure what to do - should she share the sweets with the other girl or keep them for herself? 

In the end, Sandy decided to share and split the sweets. Both of them were smiling and happy! Sandy realised that it was much better to be kind and share than to fight. She left the valley with a lesson learned.

Once upon a time there was a brave girl named Jane. She loved playing outdoors in the sunshine. One day, she went to walk along the beach. She stumbled across something curious - an empty sea! Jane could not believe her eyes. 

She took a few steps closer to the sea and saw a small fish caught in a net. Without hesitation, she jumped in and started trying to free the little fish.

"What are you doing?" asked a voice behind her.

Jane turned around and saw a friendly old man.

"I'm trying to rescue the fish," she said.

The old man smiled. "You're a brave girl!"

Together they managed to rescue the fish, set it free back into the sea, and Jane went home a happy girl.

Once upon a time there was a black cat named Pit. Pit was a very curious cat. One day, Pit decided he wanted to explore a big black pit he had seen in the yard. 

Pit's mommy saw him walking towards the pit and shouted, "No, Pit! Don't go in there!" 

But Pit was already standing at the edge of the pit, so he looked up and said, "What is down there?" 

His mommy replied, "It's a big, deep, dark pit. I don't want you to go down there, so please don't." 

But Pit couldn't help himself. He wanted to know what was down there. So he put one paw in and then another and soon he was down in the pit. It was very dark inside, so he felt around. Soon, he found a big black mouse! 

Pit was so excited that he quickly put the mouse in his pocket and climbed back out of the pit. He raced home to show his mommy the mouse. 

His mommy was so pleased with what Pit had done that she gave him a hug and said, "That was very brave of you to go in the pit, Pit!"

Andy was so excited for his first day of school. He put on his backpack and skipped all the way to the classroom. As he walked into the classroom, he heard the teacher say "Welcome! Let's start with a safe game of bounce."

Andy was so excited, he couldn't wait to try. He ran up to the middle of the room and said to the teacher, "Let me try first!"

The teacher smiled and said, "Okay then, Andy. Bounce the ball all the way around the room!"

Andy excitedly started bouncing the ball. He bounced it around all the tables and chairs in the classroom. He bounced it through the door and back around again. Andy felt very safe, even though he was bouncing alone.

When he was done, the teacher smiled and said, "Well done, Andy! You can keep bouncing around the classroom whenever it's safe to play!"

Andy smiled and bounced his way back to his seat. He couldn't wait to come back to school tomorrow!

"Tommy, let's go get the luggage," said Dad.

Tommy excitedly followed Dad outside. On the sidewalk, they saw a big truck. Dad opened the back and said, "This is the truck that is going to provide us with our luggage."

Inside the truck was a big bag. It was round and red, with many pockets on it. Dad said, "This is a warm bag, Tommy. It will keep all of our things safe."

Tommy reached out to touch the bag. He said with fascination, "Does this bag provide us with lots of things, Dad?".

Dad laughed and said, "Yes, Tommy, it does provide us with lots of things. We will be able to bring all the things we need for our trip." 

Together, Dad and Tommy loaded the warm bag onto the car. Then, they both smiled to each other and headed off on their adventure.

Once upon a time there was a great race. The racers were ready and waited for the flag to drop. When it did, off they went. Some went faster than others. As they went around the track, some were ahead and some were behind.

The racer with the new car stayed ahead the whole way. He knew he had a good chance to win. He was the fastest one there. 

Then a terrible thing happened. The new racer's car hit a rock and his car stopped. He tried really hard to push it, but it would not start again. He was so disappointed. 

The other racers went on. One of them went really fast and took the lead. He shouted out, "I'm gonna win this race!" 

But when he crossed the finish line, he saw that the racer with the new car had stayed ahead and he had won the race. 

The other racers were so disappointed, but the racer with the new car was so happy. He had remained in the lead and won the race.

Once there was a mom and a boy. The boy asked his mom to listen to some jazz. She said, "ok".

The boy put on the jazz and it made him happy. He started to dance around the room. He was so light and the music was so good.

But then something happened. His mom said it was too loud and asked him to separate from the music. The boy didn't want to, so he said no. His mom got mad and said he had to separate from the music now. The boy was sad and didn't know what to do.

Then it happened. His mom made him separate from the music. The boy was alone and felt terrible. He tried to play the music again, but his mom told him he had to stop.

The boy was so sad. He wanted to listen to the jazz and dance, but his mom said no. He knew he had to separate from the music and never listen to it again.

Jack and Jill were playing chase in the hall. Jack was running and jumping and having lots of fun. Jill got a bit careless and tipped over a flower pot. It made a crash and a mess!

Suddenly, Jill felt scared and started to cry. Jack stopped playing and went to her. He said, â€œItâ€™s ok Jill, letâ€™s clean it up.â€ He helped her clean the mess and then gave her a hug.

Jill felt better. She accepted Jackâ€™s help and the two of them were soon playing again. They were even more careful with the flower pots, so no more accidents happened.

Jack and Jill were best friends now and they played together in the hall every day. They accepted each otherâ€™s mistakes, laughed a lot and never got careless again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily wanted to find a secret so she could keep it all to herself. She searched the house until she found a key. She was so excited and opened the door with the key.

Inside the room, she found a big mess. Nothing was clean and everything was scattered about. Lily wanted to clean it all up but the mess was too big for her. She tried her best to make it mild, but she could not do it.

Lily had a secret now, but she was not happy. The mess stayed in the room and there was no way she could make it clean. She was sad, but there was nothing she could do. The secret stayed hidden and she never had her clean secret.

The sun was shining in the clear, blue sky. Down in the wild meadow, a little girl named Sarah was picking flowers. She explored the tall grass with such joy and curiosity! 

Suddenly, a mosquito sprang out of the wild grass and flew right past Sarahâ€™s ear. â€œSnap!â€ Sarah exclaimed, as she tried to swat it away with her hand. But the mosquito flew off into the grass before she could touch it. 

â€œMosquitoes are so wild!â€ Sarah said to no one in particular. But even though she had tried to swat the mosquito away, she felt a longing to try and catch it. What fun that would be!

Sarah ran around the meadow, snapping her hands and trying to catch the wild mosquito. No matter how hard she tried, the mosquito stayed just out of reach. 

But Sarah was not about to give up! She moved around the meadow again, this time with an even bigger smile. She snapped her hands, and suddenly the mosquito flew right into her hands. â€œYes!â€ Sarah exclaimed. She had finally caught the wild mosquito!

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit who liked to go on adventures. She liked to explore the world around her.

One day, the rabbit found a valley filled with different kinds of flowers. She was so excited that she started hopping around in glee.

The rabbit asked her friends, "Do you want to explore the valley with me?"

But her friends didn't want to go, so the rabbit decided to venture off alone.

As she hopped and explored the valley, she noticed something different. It seemed like something was calling her to come closer.

Suddenly, she saw a tall figure at the end of the valley. She approached the figure and it was then that realized it was a giant. 

The giant smiled warmly at the rabbit and said, "I've been waiting for you, little one. Let's rest in the valley together."

The rabbit smiled and knew that the valley was her special place. She and the giant stayed there often, talking and resting together under the stars. The rabbit's adventures were always different-- filled with joy and laughter.

Once there was a little girl called Anna. She was three years old and loved to play in the park. One day, when she was exploring, she came across a giant scale. She stepped up on the scale and it moved all the way up.

Anna was very excited and began to yell. She loved the feeling of being so high. Her mom saw what she was doing and ran over.

Her mom said, "Anna, you must come down now! You are feeling helpless on the scale!"

Anna tried to ignore her mother's words, but she knew she was right. Slowly she climbed down the scale until she was safely back on the ground.

Her mom smiled and praised her for being such a brave girl. Anna then ran off to find something else to explore.

Once there was a girl named Henry. She lived in a child's room and enjoyed painting a lot. One day, Henry wanted to paint a number. She was very anxious to see what it would look like.

When she had finished the painting, she showed it to her parents. But they said it wasn't good enough. Henry felt really bad, but she was determined to make a better painting.

The next day Henry came back with what she thought was a better painting. But her parents weren't impressed, and they said it still wasn't good enough. Henry was so frustrated, she started to cry.

Her mom comforted her and said "Henry, painting is like a journey. It's important to take your time and keep trying. It's not about the final painting, it's about the effort you put in along the way."

 Henry was sad, but she tried to take her mom's advice. She kept painting and finally made a picture her parents liked.

The moral of the story is to not be anxious when trying something new and to keep trying, even if something doesn't turn out the way you want.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who enjoyed going for a drive. He had a little car that he could drive around his neighborhood.

On this particular day, the boy wanted to go for a drive but he couldn't find his car. He asked his dad for help. Dad said, "Try looking in the garage. I think I hooked your car there last week."

The boy went to the garage and sure enough, there was his car hooked to the wall. He smiled and unhooked it. He felt excited as he drove away.

Where was the boy going? He was going to a nearby park where he heard a harmless creature was living. He was eager to find the creature!

The boy drove through the park until he spotted the harmless creature. It was a beautiful butterfly! He was so happy that he drove around the park, following the butterfly so he could watch it flutter around. 

The boy had an amazing time that day. He went on a drive, found his car, and saw the harmless creature he had been looking for. It was an adventure he would never forget.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Martin and Ellen. They were both 3 years old and were always playing together. 

One day, Martin and Ellen were playing together in the garden. But something happened that made them both very sad.

Martin had picked a flower from the flowerbed. Ellen said to him "That's not nice, you mustn't do that!" But Martin didn't listen.

Ellen's dad saw what had happened and he was very angry. He called out in a fierce voice "Martin, that was not ok! You need to be punished!"

Martin was very scared, he started to cry. He and Ellen's dad put their hands together and he said: "Martin, you must make a print of your hand with your finger, so that you will remember next time that it is not ok to pick flowers." 

Martin made a print in the soft soil as a punishment, and he promised he will never pick a flower again. 

Ellen and her dad hugged Martin and they all went inside to have a nice warm drink.

Mary was playing in her classroom when she had an idea. She was going to spoil all her classmates! She took three candy bars and started sharing them out, one bar to everyone else in her class. 

But then a teacher came in and saw what was happening. "Mary," she said, "what are you doing? You can't share out candy in the classroom."

Mary was shocked. She said, "But everyone else was going to be so happy I was sharing it."

But the teacher said, "It's not nice to be so ignorant. You could spoil everyone's appetite before lunch if you give them snacks now. Now, why don't you put the candy away?"

Mary felt really bad, but she knew the teacher was right. She put the candy away and decided that in future, she would act more kindly and not be so ignorant.

Once upon a time, there was a big mountain in the forest. It was so high. The animals loved living near the mountain, especially a squirrel family.

One day, the animals noticed something strange. Smoke seemed to be coming from the top of the mountain. It was increasing by the minute.

The animals were worried, so they went up the mountain. On the way up, they saw more and more smoke. It was getting thick in the air.

When they reached the top, they found the cause of the smoke. There was a big fire burning, and it was increasing.

The animals quickly ran back down the mountain, and the fire brigade came soon after. With their help, the fire was put out and the smoke cleared. All the animals were safe and happy.

Once upon a time, there lived a boy called Joey. He was three years old and lived in a small house with his mom and dad. 

One day, Joey's mom said "It's time to get ready to go, Joey!"

Joey replied, "I don't want to dress!" 

His mom said, "Don't make me shut the door! You need to put on your dress. It will only take a few moments."

Joey still didn't want to get dressed, so his mom said, "Listen here, young man. I'm being very persistent about this. You need to put on your dress now!"

Finally, Joey relented and put on his dress. His mom smiled and gave him a hug.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah who loved plants. She planted lots of them in the garden and took time to care for them every day.

One night, a dark storm came and all the plants got wet from the rain. When morning came, Sarah looked in the garden and saw that a dark plant was missing. She gasped and asked her mom, 
"Mommy, why is one of my plants gone?" 
Her mom said sadly, 
"Oh sweetie, sometimes things get lost during a storm. You will have to learn to accept that you lost it."

Sarah was very sad. She realised that if she had taken better care of her plants, maybe some of her plants would not have been lost.

The moral of the story is: When it comes to taking care of special things, it is important to protect and watch over them, so they don't get lost in bad storms.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Cindy. She was a very brave girl and loved adventures. One day, she went to the movies with her family. 

When Cindy entered the theatre, she suddenly heard a loud roar. She felt very nervous! Her dad reassured her, saying "Don't worry, it's just the movie." 

Cindy wasn't so sure. She asked her dad, "What kind of movie is it?" Her dad grinned and told her, "It's a monster movie - and you'll love it!" 

Cindy felt a bit better, but she was still a bit nervous. She asked again, "Will the monster roar again?" Her dad said, "Yes, probably. It's funny when it roars." 

That made Cindy feel much better. She looked forward to the movie, and sure enough, it was full of roars - both funny and scary! But Cindy stayed brave the whole time and even laughed at the monster's roars. When the movie ended, she said, "That was fun!"

Once there was a famous kite that liked to speak with the birds in the sky. Every day it would fly around and talk with them about the clouds and the wind. One day, a little girl spotted the kite and decided to fly it. She ran to the park with it under her arm and couldn't wait to get it in the air.

Once the kite was let go, it flew higher and higher and seemed to talk to the birds more excitedly than ever before. The girl watched in wonder and tried to call out to the kite, but it only spoke with the birds.

She asked one of the birds what the kite was saying. The bird responded with a cheerful chirp, "The kite says it's happy to be here with you today! It loves its new home in the sky and wants to come back and see you again soon."

The girl smiled in delight and thanked the bird before running home with the famous kite still in her heart.

"Why did the mill disappear?" asked Susie.

Her mom smiled, but her eyes were sad. "I don't know, Susie," she said.

Susie was frustrated. She loved the mill. It was her favorite place. It had the sparkling stream that she liked to play in.

On the way home, Susie asked her mom over and over again why the mill had disappeared. But each time her mom only shook her head and said she didn't know.

Finally, as they were walking up to their house, her mom stopped and said, "Sometimes things disappear, and we never understand why."

Susie's eyes were wide. "But I don't want it to disappear," she said sadly.

Her mom smiled, put her arm around Susie, and hugged her close. "I know. But it is gone, and we'll have to make new memories the best we can," she said.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called John who lived in a big house with his family. One day, John went to visit his Grandma's house. Grandma opened the door and said, "Hello John! Come in!"

John stepped inside and Grandma asked him, "Do you have anything with you, John?" John saw that Grandma had a gun on the table and he was scared. He didn't answer.

Grandma became very rude and shouted, "Answer me, John!" John suddenly remembered that he had brought a toy car, so he showed it to Grandma. 

Grandma smiled and said, "That's nice, let's play with it together." John felt much better and he happily said "Yes!"

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Joe. He was three years old and loved to write. He wrote stories about all sorts of things: animals, food, even the sky.

One day, Joe found a funny looking patch on the ground. It was a black patch and Joe knew he had to write a story about it. He ran and got his notebook, eager to start writing.

Just then, Joe's mom called out to him. She said, "Joe, what are you doing?"

Joe said, "I'm writing a story about this funny black patch!"

Joe's mom smiled. "That sounds really fun," she said.

So Joe went back to the black patch and started writing. He wrote and wrote until he had finished the story. When it was done, he was very proud of what he had written.

The End.

Once there was a little girl named Kim. One day, Kim went for a walk in the woods near her house. She looked around and saw a big, blue pool. She stepped closer to take a look. Suddenly, she heard a voice from the pool. A frog appeared on a rock in the middle of the pool.

Kim: "Hello, frog!"

Frog: "Where did you come from?"

Kim: "I stepped out of my house."

Frog: "You look very lonely. Do you want to play with me?"

Kim smiled. She stepped into the pool and soon they were playing games. Kim and the frog talked and laughed. Kim forgot how lonely she felt.

When it was time to go, Kim waved goodbye to her frog friend. She felt happier and less alone.

Moral of the story: it is important to make friends and enjoy life. Friends make us feel less lonely.

Once upon a time, there was a helpless crab who wanted to swim in the sea. She looked around and couldn't find a way to get to the water. Suddenly, she heard a voice. 

"Come here, little crab. I can help you," said the voice. The crab looked around and saw a beautiful white duck.

"Jump on my back and we'll swim to the sea together," said the duck. The crab was so happy and jumped on the duck's back. Together, they swam off to the sea.

The crab laughed as she watched the waves and felt the warm sun on her back. She knew she was safe and that the duck would look after her.

The duck and the crab swam for hours until they reached the shore. The crab thanked the duck and hopped back onto the sand.

From then on, the crab would always look back fondly on the day she had taken a ride on the beautiful duck's back and gone swimming in the sea.

The ocean was calm and beautiful. There were lots of fish in the water and they were swimming around and having a great time. Suddenly, an octopus started to splash in the water. It was so happy! The octopus was loyal to its friends, and they all wanted to hang out together. 

The octopus started to play a game with the other fish. It would splash near them, and the fish would swim away really fast. It was so funny! The fish loved the game, and the octopus was very proud of being loyal.

The fish kept swimming away from the octopus each time it splashed, but they eventually realized that the octopus was only playing. They all swam back to the octopus and surrounded it in a big circle. They started to splish and splash together and have lots of fun.

The octopus was so happy and loyal to its new friends. All the fish learned that having a loyal friend can be the best thing in the world!

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy. His name was Alex and he was three years old. Alex loved to perform special shows and put on plays.
One day, Alex asked his Mama and Papa if he could perform a special show. His Mama and Papa said yes, and Alex was so happy!
He decided to put together a show with all of his important items. He took his toys and put them in his crib. Then, he began practicing.

Mama asked, "What kind of show are you performing, Alex?"
"It's going to be the most special show ever!", said Alex, dancing around the room. 
He clapped his hands and whirled around and around. He smiled and said, "It's a surprise!"

The day of the show finally arrived, and Alex was very excited. He performed in front of his Mama and Papa and even his grandparents. They all laughed and clapped when Alex finished his show. 

Mama told Alex, "That was a very important performance. You should be proud of yourself!"
Alex smiled and said, "Can I perform this show again tomorrow?"

Timmy was sad. His baseball had rolled away to an area he couldn't reach. Suddenly a dependable friend walked up and said, "I can help you." He grabbed the ball and smiled. Timmy was so happy he forgot to say thank you. He just smiled and hugged his new dependable friend.

The two of them ran around the park throwing and catching the baseball. Timmy was having so much fun that he forgot how sad he was. His new friend was dependable, and very good at playing baseball.

After a while, Timmy's mom had to go, and his new friend had to leave too. They said goodbye and his new friend frowned. That made Timmy sad all over again. He said goodbye and waved until his friend was gone. He went home feeling lonely. 

Seeing his new friend frown made Timmy realize that he had not properly thanked him for getting the baseball. It was important for Timmy to stay grateful, so the next day Timmy sent his friend a card saying "Thank you for being dependable and helping me get my baseball".  His friend smiled and they became friends for a long time.

One day, Jane was walking through the woods searching for a place to take a nap. She had been walking for hours and was feeling very tired. All of a sudden, she spotted a tunnel. She thought it was the perfect place to take a nap and cautiously stepped inside. As soon as she sat down she felt a sense of calm and closed her eyes. Everything was peaceful until she heard a loud voice. 

"You can't take a nap here!", yelled a voice.

Jane opened her eyes and saw a squirrel standing in front of her. He continued speaking, "This tunnel is my home. You have to leave or else you will be stuck here forever." Jane was feeling frustrated but knew that the squirrel was right. She slowly began to stand up and as she stepped out of the tunnel, she thanked him for reminding her that she needed to find a better place to take her nap. 

The next day, Jane returned to the woods feeling determined to find the perfect place to take a nap. After a while, she noticed a small clearing in a nearby park. She happily ran over to the clearing and laid down in the soft grass. She quickly drifted off to sleep and felt content to have finally taken her nap in a nice and safe place.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was three years old and excited about studying.

One day she was playing with a bubble. She watched it closely and studied how it floated in the air, wide and round. "This bubble is so pretty," she said.

Suddenly, the bubble floated away. The girl ran after it to try and catch it. It was so wide and she couldn't catch up. Suddenly the wind picked up and the bubble flew away.

The little girl was sad and started to cry. But then, she saw a rainbow in the sky. She smiled and studied it closely. She thought she could reach the rainbow if she flew on the back of a bird.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer and his sheep. The farmer lived on a big farm full of dirt and mud. 
One day, the farmer was looking for his sheep but he could not find them. He looked everywhere for them but he could not see them. He was worried and started to yell.

Suddenly, he heard a loud "baa!" He looked through the mud and saw the sheep! But they were dirty! He had to get them out of the mud.

The farmer yelled at the sheep to try and get them out of the mud. The sheep started jumping and jumping. Finally, the farmer got them out safely. 

The farmer was relieved and he gave the sheep a big hug. He was so happy that the sheep were safe and not hurt. From that day on, the farmer was extra careful when watching his sheep.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends. They were Lily and Rose.

Rose said to Lily, "Do you want to come to my party?" 

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, I do! Can I bring my friend Tom? He is a good friend too."

Rose hesitated for a moment, "I don't think so. We don't have much food, and Tom might not get enough." 

"That's selfish," replied Lily. "I recommend that we invite Tom too."

Rose thought about this and she agreed. She said, "Ok, let's give him an invitation and make sure he knows how much food there will be."

So they sent Tom an invitation and all three went to the party. They had a wonderful time and ate lots of food. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a big bus. Every day, it was busy taking people to their destinations. One day, it drove to a big town.

When the bus arrived, a little girl came out. Her name was Lola. She had been on an adventure and was making her way back home.

As she walked, she met an old woman. "Good morning child," said the old woman. "What brings you here?

Lola smiled and replied, "I am returning from a very long journey. I went to a magical place and had so many adventures! I even heard a story about a beautiful princess!"

The old woman smiled and said, "That sounds like a wonderful experience. I am sure you enjoyed it."

Lola nodded in agreement, then said goodbye to the old woman and continued her journey. Over the next few days, she made her way back home, remembering the busy days on the bus and the magical stories she had heard.

One morning, Jack woke up feeling adventurous. He shouted for his mum, but she was busy. He put on his shoes and went outside.

Suddenly, Jack saw a package at his front door. He was excited, but also a bit scared. He got closer to look.

Then, the package called out to Jack!

"Hey, little Jack!" it said. "Take me with you on your adventures!"

Jack hesitated, then he decided to pick up the package and take it with him.

They explored the forest and the beach. Jack and the package had a lot of fun. Then, it started to get dark.

"It's time to return home now," said the package.

Jack sighed, but he knew it was time to go. He said goodbye to the package and went back home.

He returned with lots of stories to tell his mum.
